section_checks.assessment: Inner-wall tear, branch-flow failure, Stanford A/B and aneurysm distinction match Mayo/Cleveland. This introductory article is not automatically an entire-leaf mapping for every anatomic or rupture subclass.

Hypertension, smoking/atherosclerosis, inherited connective tissue, valve/family history, pregnancy and exertion are supported by separate institutional material. The article does not present these risks as sufficient diagnostic criteria or claim lifestyle erases inherited risk.

Mayo and Cleveland explicitly support emergency contact for abrupt severe pain or neurologic/breathing signs. South England adds maximal-at-onset history; tearing quality is optional. Passing onset/history to staff is practical information organization, not a diagnostic algorithm.

Emergency suspected acute disease, stable chronic surveillance, family screening and tolerability contacts are distinguished. The settled-pain caution is explicit in South England p3; separate sources substantiate the urgent acute pathway. No self-treatment or universal BP target is introduced.

Pulse/BP asymmetry is a possible finding rather than mandatory. Dedicated aortic CT, TEE and MRI are differentiated; MRI emergency limitations are directly explained by Cleveland. A chest film cannot provide the proposed definitive pathway on its own.
MI, aortic-wall injury, bulging aneurysm and rupture are not synonyms. Stroke may coexist with dissection. These are explanations of clinician assessment, not a symptom-based exclusion tool.

Separate US/UK sources support emergency type A repair and monitored uncomplicated type B treatment. Rupture/malperfusion drives escalation; US ACC additionally names intractable pain and hypertension. Valve and stent decisions remain anatomy-dependent.

Mayo, NHS and the added South Tees pharmacy leaflet support adverse effects and avoiding abrupt withdrawal. The added AAS original guideline excerpt plus NHS explicitly support bradycardia/heart-block selection cautions; Mayo supports asthma caution. Pregnancy medication review uses ACC/ESC without numerical self-dosing.

Mayo/NHLBI support cardiovascular food and sodium advice, not structural healing. No-food-repair is bounded to the cited treatment pathways, not a universal systematic-review claim. CKD nutrition and open-heart-surgery appetite suggestions retain those exact populations; ordinary meal organization is not a drug-level intervention.

BP logging and keeping reports are low-risk information organization. ACC/AHA official slide214 specifically addresses intense isometric/Valsalva/burst/collision activity. Cleveland independently supports moderate walking and heavy-lifting precautions. Sudden new symptoms take priority over home measurements.

ACC family guidance and Cleveland corroborate genetic/family surveillance. ACC2022 and ESC2025 independently authored guidelines address coordinated pregnancy care; ESC explicitly retains distal risk after root repair. They may share studies and are not treated as independent trials.

Mayo/Cleveland support prompt care and variable recovery; ACC/Cleveland support residual-disease CT/MRI even without pain. Follow-up timing is planned by the team, and new severe pain/neuro signs are distinguished from routine tolerability discussions.

Rupture/tamponade, brain/kidney/bowel/limb ischemia and valve leakage agree with the institutional sources. The text does not say all complications happen or borrow unqualified mortality percentages. Residual enlargement is connected to planned surveillance.

Risk modification and family screening are separated from prevention of later progression. Medicines, appropriate activity and imaging continue after repair; there is no claim of guaranteed prevention.
